Didier Dagueneau
Pouilly-Fume -  Established in 1982 in the commune of Saint-Andelain, Didier sought to do things differently. His wines revitalized the appellation & changed the expectations of a Pouilly-Fume. After his untimely passing in 2008, his children, Louis-Benjamin & Charlotte, continue his vision.

Menetou-Salon - The Domaine de l’Ermitage, nestled in the heart of the Menetou-Salon, combines modernism and tradition, for the sake of quality, and for the passion of wine.

Vignoble Ollivier Freres
Muscadet Sevre et Maine - Since the 1800s, the Ollivier family has tended to the vines here. Today two brothers, Jean-Luc & Guy, manage the operation. Their wines have crisp, citrus-like acidity and are perfect examples of the seaside terroir that they come from.

Chateau Moncontour
Vouvray - One of the oldest estates in the Loire Valley, with history tracing back to the Archbishop of Tours in the time of Saint Martin (Year 397). The Feray family has managed it’s vineyards since 1994, preserving the castle as a historical site & producing both still & sparkling wines from this estate.

Domaine Chavet
Menetou-Salon - The Chavet family has been in Menetou-Salon since the 17th century. The ancestral vineyards, handed down from generation to generation, are cultivated with the greatest respect for the vine and its environment.

OTHER FRENCH REGIONS

Chateau les Hauts D’Aglan
Isabelle Rey-Auriat took over her 14-hectare family estate in 1994, the fifth generation to tend to the vines. Her vineyard is her lifes work. The vineyards sit between the Atlantic, the Mediterranean, and the Pyrenees mountains on the highest terraces of the Cahors appellation.

Chateau Planeres
For 4 generations, the Jaubert-Noury family has tended to the vines under the Catalan sun. The red stone castle from the late 19th century overlooks the 100 hectares of vineyards planted in gravelly soil, taking deep root in the warm Mediterranean terroir.

La Cave de Roquebrun
Founded in 1967, the cellar produces Saint-Chinian-Roquebrun, Saint-Chinian, Languedoc, and Pays d’Oc. With a professional team motivated by high standards and quality, this village cultivates its independence and uniqueness.

Domaine de Papolle
The Romans the vine, the Arabs the alembic still, and the Celts the wooden cask. When these were brought together in Gascony, “Eau-de-Vie des Rois” (Spirits of the Kings) was born. In the heart of the Bas Armagnac vineyard, the origin of Domaine de Papolle goes back to the 17th century.

Domaine de L’Ermitage
The Domaine de l’Ermitage, nestled in the heart of the Menetou-Salon, combines modernism and tradition, for the sake of quality, and for the passion of wine. Bernard Clement was one of the founders of the Menetou-Salon appellation in 1959. His daughter, Laurence de la Farge, and her husband, Geraud, continued a legacy in winemaking, and in 2003, the family established Domaine de l’Ermitage. Today, their children, Antoine and Sophie, continue to run the estate.
The Domaine covers approximately 30 acres of vines in the heart of the Menetou-Salon appellation, right next to Sancerre. 80% of the vineplants are Sauvignon Blanc and the remaining 20% are Pinot Noir. All the work is done by hand.

A letter from Antoine de La Farge, Winegrower and Winemaker at Domaine Chavet
The Chavet family has been in Menetou-Salon since the 17th century. The ancestral vineyards, handed down from generation to generation, are cultivated with the greatest respect for the vine and its environment. A winegrower does not inherit the vineyard, he or she is its guardian for future generations. It is in this spirit, and with the belief that in order to obtain a great wine it is necessary to accompany and preserve nature, that the estate has, since 2002, had Terra Vitis certification, a label that certifies that the wine is produced using sustainable viticulture techniques.
Biodiversity is our priority in the vineyard. This is why we no longer use weedkillers and favour the use of grass cover and soil management techniques. In the cellar, we accompany the natural transformation of the grapes with extreme gentleness, limiting our interventions to the strict minimum, according to the daily tastings. All our wines are aged - from 6 months in vats to 18 months in amphorae and barrels - in order to reveal the depth and essence of our great terroir. We hope to have the pleasure of seeing our cuvées in your establishment soon.
Warm Regards,
Antoine
